data.narrative:
Adarga, a Series B–stage defense and security company founded by Robert Bassett Cross, has raised $26.2M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 10 comparable companies: 8 private firms in Defense & Security at Series B stage and 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $26.2M total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yields $50M. Peer-median analysis across the 8 same-sector, same-stage private comparables produces $1.1B, with the peer set ranging from $300M (low) to $3.0B (high). The five largest peers by valuation—Dream Security ($3.0B), Allen Control Systems ($2.2B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), Code Metal ($1.2B), and Twenty ($1.0B)—anchor the upper end of the comparable range.

The triangulated valuation range spans $42M (low) to $1.3B (high), with a median of $587M across the two methods. This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty about Adarga's positioning within the peer cohort. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively to actual capital deployed, while the peer-median method reflects market valuations of later-stage or better-capitalized competitors. Key uncertainties include Adarga's revenue scale, customer concentration, and competitive differentiation relative to the peer set.
